name: Fernando 2006
question: Does immediate overlapping external anal sphincter repair reduce fecal incontinence at 12 months compared with end-to-end repair after obstetric sphincter injury?

arms.label: Immediate primary overlapping external anal sphincter repair
immediate primary end-to-end external anal sphincter repair

design.population: 64 women with acute obstetric grade 3b or 3c anal sphincter injury or fourth-degree perineal tear.
design.description: Randomized trial of two primary external sphincter repairs
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Objective, Methods and Results

verdictNote: The primary fecal incontinence endpoint favored overlap at 12 months; follow-up was incomplete.
takeaway: Immediate overlapping external anal sphincter repair reduced reported fecal incontinence at 12 months compared with end-to-end repair after obstetric sphincter injury (0% versus 6/25 [24%]; P = .009).
